title: Model versioning runtime API journal
content:
Personal journal / scratchpad for a developer-facing model versioning API that integrates with the runtime.

Context and motivation:
- We need a single, predictable set of primitives for (a) publishing model artifacts that the runtime can route to and (b) changing which artifact is serving traffic for a given logical model name.
- Goals: immutability of artifacts, easy safe rollouts (canary, gradual, automatic rollback on evaluation regressions), first-class manifest to describe runtime constraints (kv-cache, quantization, padding), and minimal friction for SDK/console users to pin versions.
- Non-goals: full CI/CD build system; canonical build still lives in infra repos. This is the runtime-facing surface.

Invariants / constraints:
- Artifacts are immutable and referenced by digest (sha256). UI/SDK may show semantic labels (v1.2.0) but runtime resolves to digests.
- Manifests are small JSON blobs stored alongside the artifact (S3) and signed by a publish key. Runtime verifies signature before accepting new artifact into catalog.
- Compatibility is explicit: each manifest lists minimal runtime version, kv-cache schema id, and tokenization schema hash. Changes to any of these are breaking and must trigger prewarm/migration.

High-level API shapes (sketch):
- POST /v1/models/publish
  payload: {"name": "embedder-a", "artifact_url": "s3://.../artifact.tar.gz", "manifest": {..}, "signature": "..."} 
  returns: {"model_id": "embedder-a@sha256:...", "status":"accepted"}

- GET /v1/models/{model_name} -> returns listing of aliases/labels and resolved digest(s) and active rollout config

- PATCH /v1/models/{model_name}/pin   (pin label or digest to route)
  payload example: {"target": "sha256:abcdef..", "mode": "immediate|gradual|canary", "strategy": {"percent": 10, "window_secs": 3600}}

- POST /v1/models/{model_name}/rollout-eval
  (trigger small synthetic eval traffic against candidate; returns metrics and pass/fail policy verdict)

- POST /v1/models/{model_name}/deprecate  (mark alias as deprecated; schedule TTL)

Manifest minimal schema (text sketch; manifest itself is a JSON blob stored with artifact):
{
  "name": "embedder-a",
  "digest": "sha256:...",
  "created_by": "builder/ci/123",
  "created_at": "2025-11-03T14:22:00Z",
  "runtime_compat": ">=2.4.0",
  "kv_cache_schema": "kv-v2|hash:aa11",
  "tokenizer_hash": "tk:sha256:33ff",
  "quant_profile": "q4_0",
  "prewarm_hint": {"kv_slots": 1024, "init_prompt_prefixes": 3},
  "resources": {"gpu_mem_bytes":"15000000000", "cuda_compute_capability":"8.6"},
  "metadata": {"model_card_url":"https://...", "eval_hash":"eval-2025-10-28"}
}

Notes on semantics:
- When an alias is updated, runtime performs resolution: alias -> digest -> check manifest runtime_compat against node runtime. If incompatible, reject or queue for out-of-band migration.
- Rollouts are implemented as alias-level traffic splittings interpreted by the routing layer. Implement at ingress so warmup can happen on warm pool nodes.
- Canary mode: route small percent of real traffic + synthetic canary traffic. If regression triggers (quality drop or tokenization mismatch), automatic rollback should flip alias back.

Rollback / history model:
- All pins and alias updates are audit events. Rolling back is an alias update to previous digest. The UI should offer a one-click rollback that creates a new alias update event (never delete history).
- For breaking-change rollbacks (tokenizer/hash mismatch), include an automatic mitigation: route to a compatibility shim container that performs tokenization translation + KV adaptation for a fixed window. This is expensive, so require opt-in.

Telemetry / signals to emit:
- model.publish (model_id, owner, manifest.digest, size_bytes, quant_profile)
- model.rollout.start (from_digest, to_digest, strategy, initiator)
- model.rollout.progress (percent, nodes_warmed, avg_latency_before/after)
- model.rollout.eval (metric: perplexity/accuracy by eval_set_id)
- model.rollback (reason, triggered_by)
- model.compatibility.failed (node_id, required_runtime, node_runtime)

These names map to console dashboards and SLOs. We should standardize payload keys so the console can compute delta-latency, token-cost deltas, and quality regressions automatically.

Edge cases & implementation notes:
- Multiple identical artifacts: if same digest is republished under a new name, dedupe by digest but keep per-name metadata.
- Partial availability: when publishing, perform a preflight step that extracts prewarm_hint and places a lightweight metadata pointer into the catalog before the full artifact is copied. This allows scheduling warmers ahead of time.
- Storage concerns: manifests are small (~1KB) and signed; artifact registry stores (S3) rely on lifecycle rules and object lock for retention.
- Access control: require "publish:model" permission on branch and signature key; alias updates require "update:alias" role. All actions create audit entries with requestor identity.

CLI / SDK UX sketches:
- rw model publish --name embedder-a --artifact s3://... --manifest-manifest.json --sign-key=key1
- rw model list --name embedder-a
- rw model pin embedder-a sha256:... --mode gradual --percent 20 --window 1800

Console UX notes:
- Show alias timeline, traffic split animation (from 0->100), quick revert button, and a "safety gate" toggle to auto-rollback on eval-regression threshold breach.
- For private deployments (Private/VPC), same API surface but manifest verification uses customer KMS to verify signature, and runtime_compat check is local.

Operational playbook (brief):
- Publish artifact -> prewarm scheduled -> artifact replicated -> manifest signature verified -> set alias to candidate (canary) -> run synthetic evaluate -> open canary to small real traffic -> monitor metrics for 24h -> promote or rollback.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we permit mutable "label:*" references that point to digests and can be squashed automatically by retention rules? (pros: human-friendly; cons: additional complexity for audits)
- How to standardize tokenizer compatibility reporting? Tokenizer schema diffs are complicated; maybe require tokenizer hash and a compatibility matrix generated by our model onboarding jobs.
- Prewarm cost accounting: attribute warmup compute to publisher vs. tenant. Need billing signal in model.publish event.
- Migration tooling for kv-cache schema changes: produce adapter containers that translate cached keys on the fly during a migration window. Prototype this as a separate service.

Quick prototype manifest example (as a single-line JSON for catalog):
{"name":"assistant-1","digest":"sha256:abcd1234","runtime_compat":">=2.5.0","kv_cache_schema":"kv-v3#ff11","tokenizer_hash":"tk#9a88","prewarm_hint":{"kv_slots":2048},"quant":"q8_0","signed_by":"ci-pub-key-2","created_at":"2026-02-15T09:12:33Z"}

Closing note: this API needs to be developer-friendly (clear errors, concise CLI), ops-safe (audit, immutability), and runtime-aware (compat checks, warmup hints). Next steps: build a minimal prototype: publish -> alias pin -> canary routing -> rollback trigger. Pair with infra team on signed manifest storage and console team for audit timeline UI.
